## New Investigation Ideas
- **[2026-10-07] The live portfolio's problem is no longer a missing exit rule. It is decided exits that don't get executed. Fred wrote down this failure mode himself in AltMBA, along with a fix, and the daily briefing has no field that would show it.** [[finance/trading-portfolio]] has six positions on 🔴 Exit at once: SFM, PRX, GSK, EDEN, FLUT and, since 10-05, LULU. SFM is the clearest case. It has been on Exit since about 09-21, patience-override day 8 on 09-30, and its 10-05 deadline passed without RSI reclaiming 40. The page now says "full exit recommended, not yet executed", and the 10-06 briefing repeats "SFM full exit still outstanding" (−19%). Fred has not been inactive: the 10-01 IBKR reconciliation found four short trades opened and closed in the same window. The sales that aren't happening are of losing longs. [[learning/altmba-freds-work]] P10 records Fred's own diagnosis from 2018: "worrying too much which leads to procrastination when it's something close or personal to me". It also records his fix: "creativity is easier at a distance… adopted as a technique for avoiding procrastination on personal decisions". P12 ("I am in control of my decisions") is the decisions-vs-outcomes point that makes realising a −19% loss a decision, not a verdict. This is a different gap from the 2026-09-30 connection, which said the Patience Override has no criterion. Here a criterion fired and nothing followed. Concrete step: add an "Exit age" column to the briefing's signal table (trading days since a recommended exit was first left unexecuted), and require one line of reasoning once it passes 3 days, written as advice to a third party ("if this were a friend's portfolio…"). This applies Fred's own P10 distance technique. Back-link from altmba-freds-work's Open Question ("which lessons stuck?"): this is a live test of it.

## New Cross-Domain Connections
- **[2026-10-07] Health's main dementia source tells Fred to get the shingles vaccine because it protects against dementia. Fred owns 70 shares of the company that makes it, GSK, which is on an Exit signal, and its position note never mentions the vaccine.** [[health/source-wood-brain-sharp-2026]] lists the shingles vaccine as intervention #7 ("repeatedly appears in dementia research as protective — get vaccinated"). [[finance/trading-portfolio]] carries GSK at −8.3% on a mechanical Exit since 10-01, patience override "thesis intact (MF#33)", with a reassess by about 10-15 and earnings on 10-28. Its thesis is a Magic Formula rank. Shingrix, GSK's biggest vaccine, appears nowhere in Finance. The evidence moved in 2026, after the Wood source was written. A GSK-funded but independently designed Medicare analysis (500k+ adults aged 66+) found 24% lower dementia risk in vaccinated adults, about one case prevented per 17 vaccinated ([ScienceDaily, Aug 2026](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/08/260823015013.htm); [Boston Globe, Jun 2026](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/06/18/metro/shingles-vaccine-dementia-risk/)). GSK has also started a 33,600-person randomised trial in Finland in people aged 76+ ([Endpoints](https://endpoints.news/gsk-plans-large-study-to-see-if-shingles-vaccine-can-prevent-dementia/)). That trial is the event that would turn observational evidence into a label claim, so it is a multi-year option the Exit/Watch logic can't see. Two uses: (1) Finance: the ~10-15 reassessment and the 10-28 print should check the Shingrix sales line and any trial timeline, so "thesis intact" has substance beyond the screen rank (same gap as the 2026-09-30 connection). (2) Health: [[health/my-protocol]] is still empty. Shingrix eligibility at ~50 (and whether Fred has had it) is a one-line, evidence-tagged (`obs`, RCT pending) first entry, and the Wood page's #7 could cite the 2026 numbers.

## New Investigation Ideas
- **[2026-10-06] Fred's only open short is Oracle (5 shares, plus a $120 Dec-18 put), and its written thesis is one line: "Bearish on Oracle AI/OCI narrative." AI & Tech already has the data to turn that into a test with a pass/fail number, and the put expires within days of the next Oracle earnings report.** [[finance/trading-portfolio]] carries ORCL short at $154.55 entry ($142.30 on 10-02) and the $120 put (break-even $108.62, about 31% below the current price) with no stated thesis beyond that line. [[ai-tech/data-gpu-costs-lease-pricing-2026-08-05]] lists Oracle's on-demand H100 price at $10.00/hr. That is about 3x AWS ($3.93) and GCP ($3.00), against a market median of $2.85–3.50 that has fallen 64–75% from peak, and a neocloud breakeven of about $1.69/hr. The same page cuts the other way on one point: it finds GPU economic life *extending* (A100s still fully booked, expired H100 contracts rebooking at 95% of original price). That weakens the depreciation leg of the Burry-style AI-short case the ORCL position is labelled "partially aligned" with. [[ai-tech/data-hyperscaler-ai-revenue-2026-06-27]] gives Oracle's own target path (OCI ~$32B in FY2027, then $73B, $114B, $144B). [[finance/source-oracle-q1-fy2027-earnings]] says Q1 was on that path: IaaS $7.4B (+121%, about a $30B run rate), 300,000+ GPUs delivered in the quarter, FCF −$5B, and a $20B ATM equity raise. Concrete step: write a short idea page (or a thesis block in [[finance/models/model-oracle-cashflow-debt-rpo-2026-08-07]]) with three dated tests. (1) Implied revenue per GPU-hour: OCI IaaS revenue ÷ (estimated GPU fleet × hours in the quarter), compared with the $2.85–3.50 market median. If Oracle realises far above the market rate, the gap is the risk. (2) Q2 FY2027 OCI IaaS ≥ ~$8B, needed to stay on the $32B path. Oracle usually reports in mid-December, days before the put's 12-18 expiry, so the put is effectively a bet on this print. (3) FCF and equity issuance: a second ATM raise would confirm the financing gap that the model's Bear case ($10–15bn gap) describes. Without these tests, the position has no exit rule other than price. This is the same "thesis intact is undefined" gap the 2026-09-30 Patience Override connection found for long holdings.

## New Cross-Domain Connections
- **[2026-10-06] Burry's Micron short is filed in Finance as "memory oversupply" with no named source of the oversupply. Technology already has one: CXMT, China's state-backed DRAM maker, which is raising $8.6B at about 300x earnings and moving into HBM. A new entrant funded regardless of returns is the textbook way a memory cycle turns.** [[finance/michael-burry/index]] and [[finance/michael-burry/cross-reference]] give the MU short thesis as "Memory oversupply; AI upgrade cycle shallower than consensus". Neither names where the supply comes from. [[technology/source-semianalysis-cxmt-dram-incumbents-2026-06-23]] (SemiAnalysis) describes it. CXMT was built on ~7,000 Qimonda patents and the same buried-wordline cell the incumbents use. It recruits talent from Micron, Samsung and Taiwan, and its roadmap runs G4 → G5 → HBM. SemiAnalysis judges Micron "more vulnerable than SK Hynix given smaller HBM cushion". [[ai-tech/source-moonshot-kimi-k3-2026-07-19]] adds that CXMT is seeking an $8.6B Shanghai IPO at about an $86B valuation (~300x net profit), and that Apple is lobbying Washington so it can keep buying CXMT memory. That second detail is the part that matters: it means CXMT supply could reach Western buyers, not only Huawei's Ascend ecosystem. This sharpens yesterday's Micron/Lynch connection. There, the only bear trigger in [[ai-tech/data-hbm-supply-chain-2026-06-27]] was the three incumbents adding capacity for 2027. Capital-disciplined incumbents can slow down; a state-funded entrant with fresh IPO money has no reason to. Lynch's "cyclicals look cheapest at the peak" ([[books/book-lynch-one-up-on-wall-street]]) needs a supply shock to play out, and this is the candidate. Practical link: the through-cycle Magic Formula re-run proposed on 10-05 should use a CXMT-volume scenario for standard DRAM as its mid-cycle margin case. Burry's hub page should link the CXMT page as the named mechanism behind his short, or note that the wiki can't confirm that's his mechanism.
